To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a kissing stem-loop interaction in the 3'UTR of a viral RNA mediates cap-independent translation via a novel mechanism in which a ribosome scans the RNA and repeatedly breaks and reforms the kissing interaction.
a kissing interaction between the 5'- and 3'-UTRs mediates cap-independent translation of a viral RNA.
a long-distance kissing interaction between the 5'- and 3'-UTRs of viral RNAs facilitates 5'-end dependent ribosome scanning to initiate translation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms that regulate translation initiation by viral RNAs.
a new mechanism of long-distance RNA base-pairing that is used by viral RNAs to facilitate translation initiation.
the mechanisms of cap-independent translation, a process that is important to many viral RNAs and is also used by some cellular mRNAs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the BTE is a novel type of 5'-end- and 3'-end-dependent internal ribosome entry site.
kissing stem-loops in the BTE facilitate cap-independent translation by a scanning ribosome.
kissing interactions are not required to mediate cap-independent translation by the BTE, but are a necessary component of the mechanism that facilitates ribosome scanning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a long-distance kissing interaction can mediate cap-independent translation in a scanning-dependent manner.
kissing interactions between two stem-loop structures can mediate cap-independent translation in a 5'-end scanning dependent manner.
a kissing stem-loop interaction between the BTE and the 5'-end can mediate cap-independent translation by a scanning-dependent mechanism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the BTE is a general long-distance interaction element that can be applied in a variety of contexts to facilitate translation.
a kissing loop interaction can mediate cap-independent translation initiation, and this mechanism is not limited to the BTE.
a kissing interaction can mediate cap-independent translation in a 5'-end- and scanning-dependent manner.
